newsitem.title: USA: NFL-STEELERS AGREE TO TERMS WITH JEROME BETTIS.
newsitem.headline: NFL-STEELERS AGREE TO TERMS WITH JEROME BETTIS.

text.p: The Pittsburgh Steelers, who have been stung by a series of free agent defections over the last two years, have agreed to terms with Pro Bowl running back Jerome Bettis, the team said Monday.

Terms were not disclosed, but the television sports network ESPN reported that the deal is for four years and $14.4 million, including a $4 million signing bonus. He had turned down a four-year, $12.8 million offer from the Steelers when both sides began negotiations.
Bettis had a special clause in his contract which allowed him to become an unrestricted free agent if he rushed for more than 1,200 yards.
Bettis ranked third in the NFL with 1,431 yards last season, his first with the Steelers after being acquired from the St. Louis Rams in a draft day trade.
The reported terms of the deal would make him the third highest-paid running back in the NFL, behind Barry Sanders of Detroit and Emmitt Smith of Dallas.

The re-signing of Bettis came three days after the Steelers lost Pro Bowl free agent linebacker Chad Brown, who signed a six-year, $24 million deal with the Seattle Seahawks. Cornerback Willie Williams followed Brown when he agreed to terms with Seattle on Sunday.
The Steelers lost quarterback Neil O'Donnell, linebacker Kevin Greene and tackle Leon Searcy to free agency last season, but still managed to win the AFC Central Division with a 10-6 record.
However, Pittsburgh failed to return to the Super Bowl, falling to the New England Patriots in the divisional playoffs.
Bettis, who turned 25 on Sunday, rushed for more than 1,000 yards in each of his first two NFL seasons with the Rams. He rushed for 1,429 yards in 1993 and earned Rookie of the Year honours.
Bettis had 1,029 yards in 1994, but was bothered by ankle problems and finished with 637 yards in 1995, his last season with the Rams.
